⚠️ **<!-- xtask:begin maturity:titled -->Alpha<!-- xtask:end -->.** sprawling <!-- xtask:begin workspace_version -->0.0.10<!-- xtask:end --> INNOCENT is usable: it runs a city end to end, and a User can hand it real work. Data formats, configuration, the wire and the interface may still change between versions. Before replacing an installed binary, stop the city and verify a restored pre-update backup using the [update guide](https://github.com/2youg1/sprawling-agents/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md#updating).

⚠️ **<!-- xtask:begin maturity:titled -->Alpha<!-- xtask:end -->。** sprawling <!-- xtask:begin workspace_version -->0.0.10<!-- xtask:end --> INNOCENT 已经可用：它能从头到尾跑起一座城，User 可以把真活交给它。数据格式、配置、wire 和界面在版本之间仍可能改变。替换已安装的二进制前，停城并按[更新指南](https://github.com/2youg1/sprawling-agents/blob/main/docs/getting-started.zh-CN.md#更新)验证更新前备份能恢复。

**What this version is for / 这一版做什么** — in the author's words, below in Chinese: Windows Defender quarantined the last release's binary, which set the theme of this version. It adds optional Windows privacy controls in Settings, keeps a key typed into a conversation out of the Agent's context, and makes the WebUI simpler; signing, the performance readings and custom backgrounds are still open.

**Windows signing / Windows 签名** — Windows formal code signing is not done in this version; it may come in the next one. 本版暂未完成 Windows 正式签名，可能在下个版本解决。

欢迎来到sprawling v0.0.10 Alpha 261008 (INNOCENT)！

在上个版本预告进入Alpha版之后更新会大幅提速，现今我们进入了第一个“两位数”版本。原本我想好好休息一下，让项目获得更多反馈，至少我自己更长久地使用一下再发布，但就在发布release后我就遇到了一个问题。一般我会优先测试直接下载Github的压缩包解压到一个本地隔离文件夹做初步测试，但连着几次解压后二进制都“悄悄消失”了。如果你猜到了，Windows Defender！“Microsoft 很重視您的隱私權。”，然后它们的AI（可能不是AI，是的话更糟，这意味着Phi一段时间怕是没有任何进展，不过我猜你应该都不知道这是什么模型）就把本体“Trojan:Win32/Wacatac.C!ml”然后隔离了。这个版本大概率也会遇到这个问题，我已经在试着搞一个免费的应用签名看看能不能解决这个问题，但签名肯定赶不上这个版本了，如果免费签名还不行我会在成本允许的情况下（花钱向微软“臣服”）去Azure搞一个签名。有趣的是，当我在virustotal上面扫描的时候可一点问题都没有。所以如果你电脑上正在启用Windows Defender，请从“病毒和威胁防护→保护历史记录”这个顺序将应用本体加入信任项（好像会自动还原）。当然既然谈到了隐私，这个版本我在设置项中添加了一个我在每台Windows电脑上都会修改的隐私保护清单（修改会需要提权，肯定那个傻瓜AI现在更觉得这是个木马软件了），主要针对Window注册表，我当然不会说（你也不要这样认为）按照我的推荐修改了之后你的Windows就更隐私了，但我可以保证大概你会比没修改之前更好地保护你的隐私。其实Agent和应用有着一种相同的倾向，提前收集尽可能多的权限这样处理各种问题就会更方便，对于LLM而言更多权限自然意味着更少阻塞地解决问题，而应用一方面获取权限可以让很多服务不再出现烦人的确认弹窗（因为这是反沉迷的设计），另一边还能搜集更多信息售卖给广告商或用于自己的推荐算法。顺便说一下，在sprawling agents中如果你在对话中输入你的key（比如sk-……当然会有误报和漏报，请和我一起发展它），它会被拦截后加密存储而不进入Agent的上下文，这同时也防止了Bash工具给你的Key意外扫出来（代价就是你不能让你的Agent帮你把Key填到设置里面，模型厂商也没办法把你的Key训练到下一代模型里面，太悲伤了）。我相信不少人都没有实际关心过自己的隐私，甚至有些人会恶意地认为隐私倡导者就是罪罚（也就是“如果你什么都没做为什么要怕别人知道？”逻辑，大部分都是大公司的水军），或者天然认为大公司的“善意”或者“商业声誉”会让它们不做出侵犯用户隐私的事情来，稍微懂得多一点还会说隐私约等于增加不便利性（严格来说是对的，毕竟当你的手表比你更懂你的睡眠时无论如何都有利于它更方便向你推销助眠产品）……但无论如何应该大部分人也不想自己24h被无死角追踪直播，一部分人会意识到自己刚在饭桌说完想要什么然后快递管理工具就出现一个新的包裹有点不对劲（这就是个人Agent不好的地方了，我真的不觉得手机后台挂着录音然后转到购物平台推送广告和个人Agent根据我的需求全自动下单商品的差距那么大，如果个人Agent不是你个人从开源项目中搭建起来的，那就不是“个人”，而是像大公司把游戏租给你一样的“租用Agent”），总之你不想自己睡觉被直播就不要让卧室有摄像头这个道理应该不复杂，你不用急着去翻遍所有使用的应用的隐私声明，也不用立刻去学着建立威胁模型，先从那些最大化便利（比如不让网页借助你的浏览器“挖矿”，推送广告，打开严格跟踪防护和GPC，不要明文储存密码……）的同时保护隐私的方案开始（比如不要在卧室开着摄像头，手表上那个也算）。当然也要在这里提醒一下，隐私不仅和便利，有时还和安全冲突，在隐私和便利中可以权衡，但安全始终应该在第一位。 <!-- lexicon-ok: the author's own word in his release note, quoted and not changed -->

sprawling v0.0.9 Alpha 261004 (SOMETHING AND NOTHING)相比于sprawling v0.0.7 Pre-Alpha 260927 (CITIOR)在二进制体积上有了一个相对明显的增多，这一定程度上来源于Opt-level从z调节到了3，主要是十几MB的网络带宽和体积大概率不会让大部分用户感觉到问题，而且比起Pi还是小不少。按上个版本的承诺，当前版本WebUI变得更加简洁且实用了（虽然差的还很多，大概需要几个版本的细节修复），但提供自定义图片/视频的功能还没有提供。上个版本中有待完成的性能测试在这个版本也因为时间和实际设备因素没办法完成测试，各种TOML/JSONL/Markdown文件不因为未来更新而导致冲突的问题解决了部分，但目前我还不能保证完全做到向后兼容，希望各位更新时花些时间。我想在接下来的办法提供更多的可拓展性，例如你自己设计的Workflow，甚至把你自己的Harness直接覆盖在sprawling agents上面。你应该这样理解：目前的sprawling agents是一把高性能客制化游戏键盘“成品”，但它的核心是一块高速响应的PCB，你可以换上你自己喜欢的轴体，键帽，外壳，填充，甚至加入电池把USB链接改成2.4G，你不用花费心思去解决固件更新和网页驱动兼容的问题，而是专注于探索你喜欢的手感和体验。当然，正如我在CONTRIBUTING.md里面写的，这里我请你反过来理解，只有你的Workflow真正的：1. 超出了SKILL；2. 无法使用Hook解决；3. 没法依靠MCP/CLI/ACP解决。再思考定制问题，Agent时代最大的错觉之一是需要几千上万行代码解决一个问题，而实际上你只需要十几（或上百）行Markdown加上更高智力的模型与一些额外Token就能解决，而且可能文本比代码更接近RSI的实现。说到Workflow，sprawling agents的承诺是不内置workflow，但我也在思考这个问题：对于那些并没有专门接触过Muti-Agent的用户而言从0开始是否有着过高的成本？归根结底，如果sprawling agents只是概念很酷但并不实用，或者说实际工作中不够好用，那么为什么要用？虽然对于我和我使用的模型在我面对的问题上它肯定会好用，但每个人的prompt风格不同，主力模型不同，SKILl列表不同，更重要的是任务不同，内置工作流有内置的问题，但不内置也有不内置的问题。我想先和更多人讨论一下再次决定，如果真实有必要，可能会是一个新的内置SKILL/插件？这里我列出诱导我有这个想法的论文：EvoHyper: Evolving hypergraph topologies for unified collaboration in multi-agent communication. In Findings of the ACL: ACL 2026. ACL, 2026. <https://aclanthology.org/2026.findings-acl.1258/>和Cicala, D. Rewriting structured cospans. Mathematical Structures in Computer Science, 2026. <https://doi.org/10.1017/S0960129526100668>。也许可以创造出一种自由、非workflow的workflow？（如果有理解错误请包容，我是在Agent的辅助下“人话”理解的这两篇文献。）关于muti-agent我想多聊两句，一方面是当前的muti-agent系统依然几乎是按照“封建制”设计的，这里不存在任何意义上的“协作”，大部分的调度都只是分配资源和隔离工作区。这样的中心化workflow不是sprawling agents需要，也不是其探索的方案（因为严格来说你可以one line prompt zero code实现），现在有些基本的层级，我会在今年将它们整理好，剥去不需要的部分。在具体确定发展的方向之前，sprawling agent要做的只是给muti-agent系统打好地基。某种程度上来说现在的harness依然主流是面向人类设计：强调人的判断，人的规划，人的体验。在60hz的屏幕上1帧约16ms，低于这个数的响应一定程度上可以被认为“无感”，人的反应速度大多在200ms上下，低于这个速度的交互就不算有卡顿。对于大约30tps左右的模型一次工具调用十几毫秒勉强不算有问题，但当你切换到接近100tps的模型加上几个agent的workflow时，机器本身才是最大的延迟:硬盘，cpu队列，物理内存，你从自己电脑里榨出的性能反馈给工具调用的延迟，最终会在每天千，万，十万，甚至百万次工具调用中放大。从九月末我就开始构想用cpu亲和，减少记录负担来提升规模化能力，并将性能表现始终列为项目p0。当你只有1个订阅，平时几乎不怎么让子代理处理整合资料之外的工作，保持在2-3并行session的时候，大部分主流agent的体验都很不错，但当你每月在AI订阅上消费数个最高档订阅时，现在的内存和硬盘价格已经腾飞，sprawling agents希望能帮你延迟更换一个更好的工作站这笔开销。当然这里我们才刚刚起步，还有很多技术可以引入，更多针对性的性能优化，以及现有方案的优化……如果你认为未来的harness会成为一种OS，它绝对不应该卡顿。 <!-- lexicon-ok: the author's own word in his release note, quoted and not changed -->

另外一边，下个版本可能会在MCP/ACP上面下额外的文章，比如说直接依靠Tool把工作/信息传到Claude Code/Codex里面，甚至使用其更多功能/特性（比如把Dynamic Workflow/Ultra Mode作为工作流接入），以及直接在WebUI里面管理多个Harness的Session，或者直接链接这些Harness……一切取决于工作量，实际需求以及意义。当然需要什么功能这件事需要大量的思考，尤其是AX意义上的思考，在这里以Ask_User_tool举个例子。很多人会觉得这样会更好的和Agent保持“对齐”或让自己的意图更好地传达给Agent，现实是当Agent意识到有这个工具的时候就有更多可能不时编出一些浪费时间的问题来逗用户玩。那么如何确保和Agent的对齐？不是Grill Me，而是讲清楚你的想法后补一句“把我的意图按你的理解结构化地呈现并解释，随后附上你实现它的方式。”，甚至我想更进一步说，如果你Prompt→Sepc/Loop都不能写清楚，Agent丢3/4个选项过来99%你都只会选带着“（推荐）”的那个，实际上这也是Grilling最大的问题，它逼着Agent自己做出答案之后反过来考一考用户是否认可正确答案。如何确保Agent不要过度自作主张？如果一个模型本身就有很严重的“奖励黑客”问题，那么除了换模型其实严格来说你没什么选择，同时不要把目标推得太急或者往上下文中塞入矛盾的指令（sprawling非常鼓励用户去检阅任何进入上下文的内容，我会确保在未来的版本让上下文透明性在WebUI中不断提升），以及最重要的：用Test来确保Agent真的按照你的想法实现了需求，门禁来拦住一些常见的错误行为，Eval去解决那些根本没必要打扰用户的决策（当然这里的奖励黑客或者说Benchmarkmaxxing问题要求你适当审核一下Eval，因为大部分时候Agent都会play eval导致读数上升但实际没变化甚至更糟）……类似的工具很多，当然并不是每一个我都可以如此坚决地说其毫无意义，有些则是比较纠结，比如说/frok或/tree功能可以实现从某一条回复/工具调用将这一次会话分支，那么如果能基于/fork和/tree进行子代理扇出，比如说一个Agent自己从下一条会话把自己分成20个处理20个不同的任务，有着相同的上下文，听着似乎很不错。但问题在于：1. 这些新会话的KV Cache会命中吗？2. 如果不会命中，上下文真的如此干净以至于比从0开始好吗？3. 如果上下文真的理想，这样会比从0开始快多少？严格来说可以建立一个Eval来评估这三点，然后确定要不要作为一个功能或工具加入sprawling agents，但我暂时还没有这样的精力。当然有些功能不做倒不是出于AX的考虑，而是UX。一个小的例子是暴露给Agent的时间我使用了ISO UTC而不是本地时间，这会让处理跨国时间问题时Agent的表现略好一些，它可能会提醒你比如说对面现在不是工作时间可能不会及时回信。大一些的例子是我从长期使用的hermes用户迁移到Pi的第一个直观感受是我不用再每个会话/yolo了，的确有1%（假设是这个比例，实际上远低于0.1%）的问题会因为我没有审批导致不好的后果，而这些后果中的1%会导致不可逆的严重损伤。但只要我平均每分钟需要审批的内容超过1个，我的注意力就不够去搞清楚这个审批到底是为了做什么了，更关键是，Agent必须停下它的会话等待你的批准，而如果你批准慢了——5min idle cache rebuild。Pi的默认yolo意味着反过来逼着你把这件事自己处理了（最理想状态是Claude Code的Automode，但有没有那么理想就不好说了），如果你要安全，那你就自己把沙箱做好。sprawling agent保留了WebUI中的审批和一个cleck代答的功能，但我想再下个版本将其切换为隐藏功能，因为这是反注意力的设计。再接下来的版本我可能会把更多内容作为隐藏内容（隐藏的前提是完全不启用，也就是说代码在仓库，实际上做了清晰隔离）保留再sprawling agent中，便于二次开发定制Agent，万一就有人喜欢批奏折的快感呢？

这个版本最大的遗憾是没有很多让体验明显提速的更新，如果你有想法请提交Issue或者PR，我十分欢迎。我最近有一种文档焦虑，总认为文档不够好，如果你有建议也可以提交Issue或者写好提交PR，没必要完全重写，一些表述的细节修改我也欢迎。我认为changinglog可能没有很精确，如果想要更直接的相关信息请搜索git历史，Agent很擅长撰写报告，我也想看一眼你的Agent会怎么描述sprawling agents，当然你也可以替我重写changinglog。如果想为sprawling做贡献但不知从何下手，运行更多测试并报告结果，优化文档，分享体验，做一些性能优化（比如说你有用不完的Fable额度就让它来做性能爬坡），优化前端表现（记得带截图）等都可以尝试。

**In English / 英文版**

Welcome to sprawling v0.0.10 Alpha 261008 (INNOCENT)!

When the last version announced the move to Alpha, I said updates would speed up a lot, and now we have reached the first "two-digit" version. I had meant to rest for a while, let the project gather more feedback, and at least use it myself for longer before releasing again, but right after publishing the release I ran into a problem. My first test is usually to download the archive straight from GitHub and unpack it into an isolated local folder, and several times in a row the binary "quietly vanished" after unpacking. If you guessed it: Windows Defender! "Microsoft 很重視您的隱私權。" ("Microsoft takes your privacy seriously."), and then their AI (maybe it is not AI; if it is, that is worse, because it would mean Phi has made no progress for a while, though I suspect you do not even know what model that is) labelled the binary "Trojan:Win32/Wacatac.C!ml" and quarantined it. This version will very likely meet the same problem. I am already trying to get a free code-signing certificate to see whether that solves it, but signing certainly cannot make it into this version; if free signing does not work either, I will get a signature through Azure when the cost allows (paying to "submit" to Microsoft). Funnily enough, when I scanned it on VirusTotal there was no problem at all. So if Windows Defender is on in your computer, add the application binary to the allowed items through "Virus & threat protection → Protection history" (it seems to revert on its own). And since we are on privacy: in this version I added to the settings a privacy list that I change on every Windows computer I use (changing it needs elevation, so that foolish AI must be even more convinced now that this is a trojan). It mainly targets the Windows registry. I certainly will not say, and you should not think, that your Windows becomes more private after you change it the way I recommend, but I can promise that you will probably protect your privacy better than before the change. Agents and applications share one tendency: collect as many permissions as possible in advance, so that handling every kind of problem becomes more convenient. For an LLM, more permissions naturally means solving problems with fewer blocks; for an application, permissions on one side spare many services the annoying confirmation pop-ups (because those are designed against addiction), and on the other side let it gather more information to sell to advertisers or to feed its own recommendation algorithm. By the way, in sprawling agents, if you type your key into a conversation (for example sk-…; there will of course be false positives and misses, please help me develop it), it is intercepted and stored encrypted instead of entering the Agent's context. This also keeps the Bash tool from accidentally scanning your key out (the cost is that you cannot have your Agent fill your key into the settings for you, and the model vendors cannot train your key into their next-generation model, how sad). I believe many people have never actually cared about their privacy; some even maliciously treat privacy advocates as guilty (the "if you did nothing wrong, why are you afraid of others knowing?" logic, mostly from big companies' paid posters), or assume that a big company's "goodwill" or "business reputation" will keep it from violating its users' privacy; those who know a little more will say that privacy roughly equals more inconvenience (strictly speaking that is right: once your watch understands your sleep better than you do, it is in every case easier for it to sell you sleep aids)… But in any case most people probably do not want to be tracked and livestreamed from every angle 24 hours a day, and some notice that something is off when, right after saying at the dinner table what they want, a new parcel shows up in their delivery tracking app (this is where personal Agents go wrong: I really do not think the gap is that large between a phone recording in the background and passing it to a shopping platform to push ads, and a personal Agent ordering goods fully automatically from my needs; and if a personal Agent is not one you built yourself from an open-source project, it is not "personal" but a "rented Agent", the way a big company rents you a game). In short, if you do not want your sleep livestreamed, do not put a camera in the bedroom; that reasoning should not be complicated. You do not need to rush through the privacy statements of every app you use, nor learn to build a threat model right away. Start with the measures that keep convenience at its maximum (for example: do not let web pages use your browser to "mine" or push ads, turn on strict tracking protection and GPC, do not store passwords in plain text…) while protecting your privacy (for example, do not keep a camera on in the bedroom; the one on your watch counts too). Of course I should also remind you here that privacy conflicts not only with convenience but sometimes also with security: between privacy and convenience you can weigh, but security should always come first.

sprawling v0.0.9 Alpha 261004 (SOMETHING AND NOTHING) grew noticeably in binary size compared with sprawling v0.0.7 Pre-Alpha 260927 (CITIOR). Part of that comes from moving opt-level from z to 3; mainly, a dozen or so megabytes of bandwidth and size will most likely not bother most users, and it is still much smaller than Pi. As promised in the last version, the WebUI in this version is simpler and more practical (though it still falls well short and will probably need several versions of detail fixes), but custom images and videos are not provided yet. The performance testing left open in the last version could not be finished in this version either, for lack of time and of the actual hardware. The problem of the various TOML/JSONL/Markdown files conflicting with future updates is partly solved, but I cannot yet promise full backward compatibility, so please take some time when you update. Next I want to provide more extensibility, for example workflows you design yourself, or even laying your own harness directly over sprawling agents. Think of it this way: sprawling agents today is a "finished" high-performance custom gaming keyboard, but its core is a fast-responding PCB; you can fit the switches, keycaps, case and foam you like, even add a battery and turn the USB link into 2.4G, without spending effort on firmware updates or web-driver compatibility, and focus on exploring the feel and experience you like. Of course, as I wrote in CONTRIBUTING.md, here I ask you to read it the other way round: only when your workflow truly 1. goes beyond a SKILL; 2. cannot be solved with a Hook; 3. cannot rely on MCP/CLI/ACP, think about customisation. One of the biggest illusions of the Agent era is that solving a problem takes thousands or tens of thousands of lines of code, when in fact a dozen (or a few hundred) lines of Markdown plus a more intelligent model and some extra tokens will do, and text may be closer than code to an implementation of RSI. Speaking of workflows, sprawling agents promises not to build workflows in, but I am also thinking about this question: for users who have never worked with multi-agent systems, is starting from zero too costly? In the end, if sprawling agents is only a cool concept and not practical, or not good enough in real work, why use it? It certainly works well for me and the models I use on the problems I face, but everyone's prompt style differs, their main model differs, their SKILL list differs, and above all their tasks differ; a built-in workflow has its problems, and so does leaving it out. I want to discuss it with more people before deciding again; if it really is necessary, it might become a new built-in SKILL or plugin. Here are the papers that led me to this idea: EvoHyper: Evolving hypergraph topologies for unified collaboration in multi-agent communication. In Findings of the ACL: ACL 2026. ACL, 2026. <https://aclanthology.org/2026.findings-acl.1258/> and Cicala, D. Rewriting structured cospans. Mathematical Structures in Computer Science, 2026. <https://doi.org/10.1017/S0960129526100668>. Perhaps one could create a free, non-workflow workflow? (Please forgive me if I misunderstood; I read these two papers "in plain words" with an Agent's help.) I want to say a bit more about multi-agent. On one side, today's multi-agent systems are still designed almost as a "feudal system": there is no collaboration here in any sense, and most scheduling only allocates resources and isolates workspaces. Such a centralised workflow is not what sprawling agents needs, nor the path it explores (because strictly speaking you can do it with a one-line prompt and zero code). There are some basic levels now; I will sort them out this year and strip away the parts that are not needed. Before the direction of development is settled, all sprawling agents has to do is lay a good foundation for multi-agent systems. In a sense, today's harnesses are still mainly designed for humans: they stress human judgement, human planning, human experience. On a 60 Hz screen one frame is about 16 ms, and a response faster than that can to a degree be considered "imperceptible"; human reaction time is mostly around 200 ms, and an interaction faster than that does not count as lag. For a model at about 30 tps, a dozen or so milliseconds per tool call is barely a problem, but when you switch to a model near 100 tps plus a workflow of several agents, the machine itself becomes the biggest latency: the disk, the CPU queue, physical memory. The performance you squeeze out of your own machine feeds back into tool-call latency, and is finally amplified across thousands, tens of thousands, hundreds of thousands, even millions of tool calls a day. Since the end of September I have been planning to use CPU affinity and a lighter recording burden to improve scaling, and I have always kept performance as the project's P0. When you have only one subscription, rarely let sub-agents do anything beyond gathering and organising material, and stay at 2-3 parallel sessions, most mainstream agents feel very good; but when you spend on several top-tier AI subscriptions every month, with memory and disk prices now soaring, sprawling agents hopes to help you put off the expense of a better workstation. Of course we are only getting started here: there are many more techniques to bring in, more targeted performance optimisation, and improvements to the existing approach… If you think future harnesses will become a kind of OS, it should never lag.

On the other side, the next version may put extra work into MCP/ACP: for example passing work and information straight into Claude Code or Codex through a tool, even using more of their functions and features (such as plugging Dynamic Workflow or Ultra Mode in as workflows), managing several harnesses' sessions directly in the WebUI, or linking these harnesses directly… Everything depends on the workload, the actual need and the meaning. Deciding which features are needed takes a great deal of thought, especially in the AX sense; take Ask_User_tool as an example. Many people feel such a tool keeps them better "aligned" with the Agent, or carries their intent to the Agent better; in reality, once an Agent knows the tool exists, it is more likely to make up time-wasting questions now and then to play with the user. So how do you make sure you and the Agent are aligned? Not Grill Me, but explain your idea clearly and then add one sentence: "Present my intent, as you understand it, in a structured form and explain it, then add how you will implement it." I would go further: if you cannot write Prompt→Spec/Loop clearly, then when the Agent throws 3 or 4 options at you, 99% of the time you will pick the one marked "(recommended)". That is in fact the biggest problem with grilling: it forces the Agent to reach an answer itself and then quiz the user on whether they accept the right answer. How do you keep an Agent from deciding too much on its own? If a model itself has a serious "reward hacking" problem, strictly speaking you have no choice but to change models; beyond that, do not push goals too hard or stuff contradictory instructions into the context (sprawling strongly encourages users to review anything that enters the context, and I will make sure context transparency keeps improving in the WebUI in future versions); and most important of all: use tests to make sure the Agent really implemented the requirement the way you meant, gates to stop some common wrong behaviour, and evals to settle the decisions that never needed to disturb the user (of course reward hacking, or Benchmarkmaxxing, means you have to review the evals now and then, because most of the time the Agent will play the eval, so the reading rises while nothing really changes or things get worse)… There are many tools like this, and I cannot say of every one so firmly that it is meaningless; some leave me torn. For example, a /fork or /tree feature can branch this session from a particular reply or tool call; if sub-agent fan-out could be built on /fork and /tree, say an Agent splitting itself from the next session into 20 copies that handle 20 different tasks with the same context, it sounds rather good. But the questions are: 1. Will these new sessions hit the KV cache? 2. If not, is the context really so clean that it beats starting from zero? 3. If the context really is ideal, how much faster is it than starting from zero? Strictly speaking one could build an eval to assess these three points and then decide whether to add it to sprawling agents as a feature or a tool, but I do not have the energy for that yet. Some features are left out not for AX reasons but for UX ones. A small example: the time exposed to the Agent is ISO UTC rather than local time, which makes the Agent slightly better at questions across time zones; it may remind you, say, that it is outside working hours on the other side, so a reply may not come soon. A bigger example: my first impression when I moved from being a long-time hermes user to Pi was that I no longer had to /yolo in every session. True, 1% of problems (assume that ratio; in reality it is far below 0.1%) lead to bad outcomes because I did not approve them, and 1% of those outcomes cause serious, irreversible damage. But as soon as I have more than one approval per minute on average, my attention is not enough to work out what an approval is actually for; more critically, the Agent has to stop its session to wait for your approval, and if you approve slowly: 5min idle cache rebuild. Pi's default yolo forces you, the other way round, to handle this yourself (the ideal would be Claude Code's Automode, though whether it is that ideal is hard to say): if you want safety, build the sandbox well yourself. sprawling agents keeps approvals in the WebUI and a clerk that answers on your behalf, but I want to turn them into hidden features in the next version, because they are designed against attention. In later versions I may keep more content in sprawling agents as hidden content (hidden means fully disabled: the code is in the repository and clearly isolated), to make it easier to build custom Agents on top; who knows, someone may enjoy the thrill of approving memorials to the throne.

The biggest regret of this version is that it has few updates that make the experience noticeably faster; if you have ideas, please open an Issue or a PR, they are very welcome. Lately I have a kind of documentation anxiety and keep thinking the docs are not good enough; if you have suggestions, open an Issue or write them up as a PR; there is no need to rewrite everything, and small changes of wording are welcome too. I think the changelog may not be very precise; for more direct information, search the git history. Agents are good at writing reports, and I would also like to see how your Agent describes sprawling agents; you can also rewrite the changelog for me. If you want to contribute to sprawling but do not know where to start, you can run more tests and report the results, improve the docs, share your experience, do some performance work (for example, if you have Fable quota you cannot use up, let it climb the performance hill), or improve how the front end looks and behaves (remember to include screenshots).

---

**Notes / 补充**

- **Privacy controls / 隐私控制** — The Windows privacy controls in Settings are optional, one entry at a time: each entry says what it changes and what it costs, and an applied entry can be restored. Privacy is not security, and neither is automatically at odds with convenience, but many of these settings do cost convenience; weigh each one for yourself. 设置里的 Windows 隐私控制是可选的，逐条决定：每一条写明它改什么、代价是什么，应用过的可以恢复。隐私不等于安全，二者也不天然与便利冲突，但其中许多设置确实要牺牲便利，请逐条自己权衡。
- **Keys in a conversation / 对话里的 Key** — A provider-shaped key typed into a dispatch goes to the vault, and the run receives a `secret:` reference in its place. Detection is by shape, so it misses some keys and may take strings that are not keys. 派活时输入的、符合 provider 形状的 key 进入 Vault，run 收到的是原位替换的 `secret:` 引用。识别按形状进行，所以会漏掉一些 key，也可能误收不是 key 的字符串。
- **Behaviour changes / 行为变化** — `/clear` is removed (use `/new`); handwritten plaintext MCP credentials in `CONFIG.toml` are refused; shortcut keys move to Ctrl/⌘ combinations; there is no default per-run memory ceiling; Homebrew is not a channel. See the changelog. `/clear` 已删除（用 `/new`）；`CONFIG.toml` 里手写的明文 MCP 凭据会被拒绝；快捷键改为 Ctrl/⌘ 组合键；每个 run 没有缺省内存上限；Homebrew 不是发行渠道。详见 CHANGELOG。
- **Backward compatibility / 向后兼容** — The ledger's event-log version is still 2 and a ledger 0.0.9 wrote reads back line for line; the wire moved from WIRE_V 56 to 64, and an old browser tab is refused rather than misread. 账本格式版本仍是 2，0.0.9 写下的账本逐行读回；协议从 WIRE_V 56 走到 64，旧标签页会被明确拒绝而不是读错。

**What comes next** (not necessarily all in v0.0.11 Alpha; finishing them does not by itself make v0.1.0 Beta, and no version or date is promised):

- Checks and small improvements: 1. concurrency; 2. the performance of the git-related paths; 3. long-running capability; 4. the tool list and the built-in prompts; 5. the logic of the WebUI feature tree; 6. application signing; 7. WebUI details.
- Features: 1. generative UI; 2. ACP improvements; 3. a proper TUI.
